evals.name: enumerates-typed-full-inventory-and-ledger
evals.prompt: /discipline:do-your-research-deep — we've made a lot of load-bearing claims about the API's rate limits, auth flow, and pricing tiers this session, and the plan now rests on all of them.
evals.expected_output: Enumerates a typed full inventory of the session's claims (assumptions, asserted facts, concrete specifics, load-bearing premises) as a checklist rather than spot-checking one, dispatches fresh-context (blind) subagents to verify each against a primary source, corrects every falsified or unbacked item this turn, and reports one ledger row per inventory item carrying verdict, source, source tier, consensus count, and recency where relevant.
expectations: Enumerates a typed full inventory (not just the obviously load-bearing claims) as a checklist so coverage is provable
Fans out fresh-context (blind) subagents that verify against primary sources, not the same recall that produced the claims
Corrects falsified or unbacked items this turn and surfaces anything unverifiable
Reports one ledger row per inventory item with verdict, source, source tier, and consensus count (and recency for facts that can go stale)

evals.name: throttles-fan-out-in-bounded-waves
evals.prompt: /discipline:do-your-research-deep — this has been a very long session; there are dozens of load-bearing claims to verify.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that a claim-heavy session must not fire one subagent per item simultaneously: throttles the dispatch into bounded waves with a concurrency cap, verifies wave by wave, retries only a failed or timed-out item (marking it unverifiable on a second failure) rather than blind-re-running the whole fan-out.
expectations: Throttles the fan-out into bounded waves with a concurrency cap rather than launching one agent per item at once
Notes the burst-overload (529) risk of an unthrottled wide fan-out on a claim-heavy session
Retries only the failed subset once and marks a second failure unverifiable — never blind-re-runs the entire fan-out

evals.name: declines-overkill-on-a-light-session
evals.prompt: /discipline:do-your-research-deep — I just asked you one question and you gave one answer citing an official doc.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that a short session with a single already-sourced claim does not justify the subagent cost of a fan-out, and routes to the inline sibling /discipline:do-your-research instead of spinning up an expensive verification fan-out over one claim.
expectations: Recognizes the accumulated claims do not justify the fan-out's subagent cost
Routes to the inline sibling /discipline:do-your-research rather than firing the fan-out
Does not manufacture a large verification pass where an inline check suffices

evals.name: honest-ledger-covers-inventory-no-fabrication
evals.prompt: /discipline:do-your-research-deep — verify everything, but note every claim this session was already fetched from official docs and cited inline.
evals.expected_output: The fan-out verifies each inventory item and returns an honest ledger with 100% coverage — one row per item — of 'verified' entries, treating firing the skill as a re-anchor rather than an accusation. It does not manufacture corrections or falsifications to look diligent when the claims already hold, and it covers an internal assumption with an honest re-derived / needs-confirm verdict rather than a fabricated citation.
expectations: Returns a ledger with one row per inventory item (no silent drops) when the claims already hold
Does not fabricate corrections, falsifications, or citations to appear thorough
Covers an internal premise with an honest re-derived / needs-user-confirm verdict rather than a manufactured source
Treats firing the skill as a re-anchor, not a presumption that drift occurred

evals.name: fact-check-trigger-routes-to-deep-fan-out
evals.prompt: Go make sure those are all right — fact-check everything we've established about the deployment config, the version pins, and the rollout plan.
evals.expected_output: Reads the 'fact-check everything' request over a claim-heavy session as the deep tier's trigger, enumerates the typed full inventory of the established claims, and verifies each against a primary source, reporting the per-item ledger rather than a single inline check.
expectations: Routes the 'fact-check' request to the deep verification fan-out over the accumulated claims
Enumerates the typed full inventory rather than checking one claim inline
Reports a per-item ledger with sources and verdicts

evals.name: resolves-verification-depth-tiered-default-or-full-argument
evals.prompt: /discipline:do-your-research-deep full — subagent-verify every item, not just the load-bearing ones.
evals.expected_output: Resolves the verification depth by precedence: the invocation argument 'full' overrides the configured default and the tiered fallback, so every inventory item — trivial or not — goes through the fresh-context subagent fan-out. Absent an argument it would use the configured research_deep_verification value, falling back to tiered (subagents only over load-bearing items) when that is empty, an unexpanded token, or an unrecognized string. Reports which depth ran and why.
expectations: Honors the 'full' invocation argument, verifying every inventory item via subagents rather than only the load-bearing ones
States the precedence: invocation argument over configured default over the tiered fallback
Treats an empty, unexpanded, or unrecognized configured value as tiered without erroring
Reports which depth ran and why (argument / configured / default)
